To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The evaporite deposition in the northern part of Carpathian Foredeep occurred during the late Badenian (ca. 13.6 ± 0,07 Ma).
the Badenian Salinization Crisis in the northern Carpathian Foreland ended before 13.06 Ma.
the Badenian Salinization and the Badenian-Sarmatian Extinctions took place in the Central Paratetthys Basin during the late Serravallan (13.6–13.1 Ma).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chronostratigraphic position of the evaporites and the overlying Pecten Beds within the NN 6 zone.
the chronostratigraphical framework of the Miocene in the northern part of Polish Carpathian foredeep.
the chronostratigraphy of the Miocene of the Carpathian Foreland, and the Badenian Saline Crisis, which was a major event in the history of the Central Parathetys Basin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Badenian Saline Crisis began after 13.80 ± 0,08 Ma, that the evaporite deposition ended before 13.06±0.11 Ma, and that the extinction of typical Badenian faunal components took place before 13.05±0.11Ma.
the evaporitic Krzyzanowicze Formation and the marly Pecen Beds are of Serravallia age, and that the Badenian/Sarmatian boundary is placed at the base of NN 6.
the evaporite deposition took probably place at ca. 13–13.4 Ma, while the Badenian faunal extinction and subsequent Sarmatian faunal diversification probably began shortly after 12.95 ± 0,11 Ma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Badenian salinity crisis ended and the post-evaporite normal marine conditions began in NN 6.
the Badenian Saline Crisis and the associated Badenian– Sarmatian Extinctions in the Carpathian Foreland took place in the late Serravalllian.
the Badenian salinity crisis in the Polish Carpadhian Foredeep lasted from ca. 13 to 12 Ma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Paratethys Salinity Crisis was a short-lived event, which took place in less than 1.7 million years.
the Sarmatian is a valid stratigraphic unit, which is characterized by the appearance of endemic S. carpathica and the disappearance of the stenohalines.
the Sarmatian faunal extinction and the subsequent Paratethys salinity crisis took place within a relatively short interval of time.
